clue.text: No brave complexion?

parts.note: a 'brave' is a Native American warrior in old westerns; the skin colour of someone who is not one of them, as such warriors named white settlers

explanation.surface: A question about someone whose looks lack courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' reads as an adjective (courageous), but here it is the noun for a Native American warrior; the term was what such warriors were said to call white people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was the westerns' term, put in the mouths of Native Americans, for a white settler with a light skin unlike their own.

clue.text: A royal pair on cine production

indicators.note: a film production makes something new, so the letters of cine are reworked

explanation.surface: A couple of royals appear in a film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair' gives its standard abbreviation, and 'production' signals a reworked film word; 'A royal' looks like the subject of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's son is a member of a royal family.

clue.text: Sort of tricky question ready to be fired

definitions.meaning: a question built to trap, carrying an assumption
a gun with a cartridge in the chamber

explanation.surface: A tricky question is fired off like a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap question carries hidden weight, and a gun with ammunition inside is primed to shoot.

clue.text: Disorientated in fast and becomes feeble

indicators.note: someone disorientated has lost their bearings, so these letters lose their order

explanation.surface: Someone fasting becomes confused and weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Swooning or growing weak, as in 'faints away', is the sense; the verb is in the third person.

clue.text: Pipe Washington wanted when he became a famous feller?

definitions.text: Pipe Washington wanted when he became a famous feller?

parts.words: Pipe Washington wanted when he became a famous feller?
parts.note: the legend has young George Washington chopping down a fruit tree; a tobacco pipe can be made from that tree's timber

explanation.surface: Asking what tobacco pipe George Washington craved when he grew famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like 'fellow' but means one who fells trees; the story says young Washington cut down his father's fruit tree and could not tell a lie about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber of the fruit tree in the Washington legend is used for tobacco pipes.

clue.text: Fishmonger on the way up?

definitions.meaning: a fish seller strips the scales from fish before sale
a climber is one who scales a wall or peak

explanation.surface: A fish seller apparently rising in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb scale: removing fish scales, or climbing up a height.

clue.text: Residential street less full than Half Moon Street

definitions.text: Residential street less full than Half Moon Street

parts.words: Residential street less full than Half Moon Street
parts.note: a curved terrace of houses, and the shape of the moon when under half lit

explanation.surface: A housing road compared with London's Half Moon Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Half Moon Street is a real Mayfair street; the moon less full than half is a thin curved sliver, a shape also given to curved rows of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved row of houses takes its name from the thin sliver of moon seen before the half phase.

clue.text: Alum thrown around set fire to flowering tree

indicators.note: the mixed letters go round the outside of the fire word
something thrown is tossed about, so the letters of alum are mixed up

parts.note: to burn something is to set fire to it

explanation.surface: A chemical is tossed about to light up a tree in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators work in turn: 'thrown' mixes up the chemical's letters, then 'around' wraps them, split two and two, about the fire word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree with hanging yellow blossom clusters, common in gardens.

clue.text: Dead or is tottering on the verge

indicators.note: a tottering figure staggers unsteadily, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone collapses by the edge of the road, dead or about to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tottering' rearranges DEAD OR IS. 'on the verge' suggests 'about to', but the verge is the grass beside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The verge is the grassy strip along the edge of a road.

clue.text: Visualises mature insects

definitions.meaning: an imago is an adult insect after metamorphosis; this is its Latin plural

explanation.surface: Someone pictures fully grown bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb for forming mental pictures; the other is the plural of imago, the adult stage of an insect.

clue.text: Braise served up in Yugoslavia

indicators.note: food served up has been prepared and turned out, so the letters of the cooking word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A braised dish is put on the table somewhere in the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns BRAISE into a new order; the definition leans on the time when the country was the core of the old Yugoslav federation.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade's republic was the leading part of the former Yugoslavia, so the part stands loosely for the whole.

clue.text: Being a variation of rate in sue cessful medical treatment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for a successful treatment

parts.note: a cure is treatment that works

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters of the word rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature is described as some altered fee within a therapy that worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb joining the clue together, but it is the noun definition; 'a variation of' and 'in' do the work, the jumbled fee placed after the first letter of the treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A living being or animal is a synonym, as in 'a creature of habit'.

clue.text: Slashes with the bat

definitions.meaning: cuts or gashes with a blade
a cricketer makes runs with the bat, i.e. totals of runs

explanation.surface: A violent swing of a cricket bat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter scores runs; the clue's second half is a cryptic way of saying what a batter does.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to cut lines into a surface, and also to make runs or points in a game.

clue.text: Diplomacy requires a royal barge maybe

definitions.meaning: the skill of managing affairs between nations
a ceremonial vessel used on official occasions, a state boat

explanation.surface: Diplomacy needs a royal barge.
explanation.definitionFit: Governing skill is the art of running a nation; read as two words it is a ceremonial vessel of the crown.

clue.text: Deceitful as the mouth of the serpent

definitions.text: as the mouth of the serpent
definitions.meaning: a snake's tongue is forked into two prongs

explanation.surface: The snake of Eden's lying speech is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying one thing and meaning another is double-dealing; and a snake's forked tongue literally splits in a pair.

clue.text: It aged at being shaken, badly shaken

indicators.note: shaking jumbles contents, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something grew old through being jolted about.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset or disturbed, flustered and nervous.

clue.text: Before 1001 iron was carried by nine of the women

indicators.note: the iron symbol comes ahead of the Roman number
in a down entry the earlier letters sit on top of the next piece, borne by it

parts.note: FE is the chemical symbol for iron
MI is 1001 in Roman numerals: M is 1000, I is 1

explanation.surface: A tale of iron borne by nine people before the year 1001.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'was carried by' means the earlier pieces sit above, on top of, the later one.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or characteristic of women is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: One who gives evidence at or after he

annotationWithheld.why: 'One who gives evidence at or after he' (8): ATTESTOR is AT + TEST + OR, but nothing in the clue gives TEST ('he' cannot); the clue looks misprinted and no source gives the original
annotationWithheld.clue: One who gives evidence at or after he

clue.text: Get car scattering oats with winter top-dressing

indicators.note: seed is scattered on a field, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer drives out to spread oats on the fields in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattering' rearranges GET CAR and OATS together. 'top-dressing' sounds like manure on a field, but it is overcoats worn on top in cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy overcoats are worn over everything else when the weather turns cold.

clue.text: Coal bin is a hazard when ap preaching a hole

definitions.meaning: a large container for storing coal or fuel

definitions.text: a hazard when ap preaching a hole
definitions.meaning: a golf sand trap near the green

explanation.surface: A coal store turns out to be an obstacle on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a sand trap guarding the green is a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fuel store, and in golf a sand-filled pit set as an obstacle.

clue.text: So male arousing she was in Herod's time!

indicators.note: arousing stirs things up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man so stirred up in the court of Herod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arousing' rearranges SO MALE. The Biblical dancer aroused Herod with her dance and won John the Baptist's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The daughter of Herodias danced for King Herod and asked for the Baptist's head as a reward.

clue.text: English flower always found in polar regions

indicators.note: the word for always is placed inside the polar letters

parts.note: S and N stand for the south and north poles
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: A flower that always grows near the poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword for something that flows, a river; this is Britain's longest, rising in Wales and flowing through England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, so it is a 'flow-er'; this one runs through the west of England into the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Army commanded followed closely

annotationWithheld.why: 'Army commanded followed closely' (6): TAILED is TA + I + LED, but no clue word gives the I; the clue seems to have lost a word ('Army I commanded') and no source gives the original

clue.text: Sky-pilot! Correct

annotationWithheld.why: 'Sky-pilot! Correct' (8): the clue is a pun ('a curate!' said aloud gives ACCURATE) with no word signalling the sound-alike, only the exclamation mark, so the homophone has no indicator

clue.text: Try hit composed for number played at Rugby

indicators.note: something composed has been put together in an arranged form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hit song is written about scoring a try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges TRY HIT. Rugby Union fields fifteen a side, so the total on the pitch is the number wanted; Rugby is also the school where the game began.
explanation.definitionFit: Two teams of fifteen make the full count of players in a Rugby Union match.

clue.text: Mainstay of the spinal column?

definitions.meaning: the vertebrae running down the body

explanation.surface: Asking whether the chief support is the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is literally the body's support, and figuratively a firm character or chief strength.

clue.text: Dull air will take in just one listener

annotationWithheld.why: 'Dull air will take in just one listener' (6): DREARY is DRY around EAR, but 'air' gives no DRY and nothing else does; the clue seems misprinted and no source gives the original
annotationWithheld.clue: Dull air will take in just one listener

clue.text: Way to encourage big fish

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
to urge on is to spur or encourage

explanation.surface: A method of cheering on a large fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea and river fish, source of caviar.
